Inventory Allocation Using Pointer Arithmetic

Problem Statement:
You are working on an inventory management system for a warehouse. The warehouse has multiple sections, each with its own stock levels for different types of items. You need to allocate space for new items based on the current inventory. Each section is represented as a continuous block of memory that holds the stock levels of different item categories.

Task: Write a C program that accepts the number of sections and the number of categories of items in each section. The program will then accept stock levels for each category in every section. You need to update the stock levels of each section by adding a specific quantity (allocated via user input) to all categories in that section using pointer arithmetic. Finally, print the updated inventory for each section.

Input Format:
The first line contains an integer whose name is S (1 <= S <= 1000) representing the number of sections.
The second line contains an integer C (1 <= C <= 100) representing the number of categories per section.
The next S * C lines contain integers representing the current stock levels for each category in every section.
The next line contains an integer X (1 <= X <= 10000) representing the quantity to be added to each category of each section.

Output Format:
Output the updated stock levels for each section, one section per line. Each section's stock levels should be space-separated.
